digest.component_or_area: Jira reconciler baseline advancement and field arbitration
propositions: Operator local status changes (reopens, un-claims) are silently reverted by the reconciler when they revert to a pre-push baseline value, because the baseline is advanced from the pass-start snapshot before outbound apply rather than after it, leaving the baseline one pass behind rebar's own outbound writes.

The baseline advance must be gated on per-mutation success, not pass-level exit code, because status transitions can soft-fail (RuntimeError from illegal reverse transitions) while the pass still exits 0, and a falsely-advanced baseline would mask genuine divergence and not self-correct.

The guard `local == baseline` → `local unchanged` has a false premise for exactly one pass after rebar pushes a field value, because the baseline holds the pre-push value while Jira holds the post-push value, causing inbound to clobber a revert-to-prior-value as if it were a Jira-side edit.

All five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) share the same `_suppressed_by_inbound` arbitration guard and therefore all expose the same ABA vulnerability, not status alone.

The fix overlays successfully-applied outbound mutations onto the pass-start snapshot before baseline advance, so the baseline becomes last-synced rather than last-fetched, restoring ADR 0026's own definition and closing the one-pass ABA window.
